title: Site-specific inhibition of translation initiation via 2'-O-methylation.
data_url: https://github.com/arangolab/2O-me_initiation_2026 (code + derived tables, archived at Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.18274765, CC-BY-4.0); sequencing data GEO GSE341562

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Cloned the authors' GitHub/Zenodo repository (21 MB) and opened every tabular file: HeLalocation0based_filtered.bed (23,753 2'-O-methylation sites + header; columns chrom/start/end/gene/consequence/strand, NO modification-ratio column), AllC42sites0based_filtered.bed (24,272 sites), mlmHeLaCognates.bed (841 rows), AllC42Cognates.bed (1,156 rows), 5UTRNmPlus1Sites.xlsx (151 HeLa + 181 C4-2 + 65 shared 5'UTR sites, with a methylation ratio column), Table_S3_PMID_35679869.xlsx 'All_P-sites' (23,327 rows x 11 columns, 0 missing values, 0 duplicate psite_id, ribosome-profiling initiation-site counts in wild-type and knockout), utr.fa (8,084 5' untranslated region sequences; 7,964 transcript IDs overlap the P-site table), 5utrCodonCounts.csv (63 rows), pos1CodonFreqHELANANO.txt (48 rows). Checked GEO: GSE341562 contains only 2 HeLa samples with bigWig coverage tracks, GSE341562_RAW.tar = 465 MB (over the 50 MB cap, metadata only). Confirmed the Zenodo deposit is code only (7.7 MB zip).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: All of the paper's own measurements (NanoLuc luciferase luminescence and green fluorescent protein flow cytometry for 2'-O-methylation at each Kozak-sequence position, n = 3-4 replicates; RTL-P validation of 12 candidate sites) come from the figures and methods text only - Europe PMC's supplementary-files endpoint timed out twice, so the supplement (Supplementary Tables S1-S7) was not retrievable and no machine-readable source-data table was seen.

a1_downloadable.note: Code and derived tables download freely from GitHub/Zenodo (CC-BY-4.0) and I cloned them; GEO GSE341562 is public. Only the journal supplement was unreachable (Europe PMC endpoint timed out twice).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The paper's actual measurement - protein output when a specific nucleotide near the start codon carries a 2'-O-methyl group - is not a column in any downloadable file; it exists only as bar charts in Figures 2-3, so it would have to be read off figures or re-measured.

a3_inputs_present.note: Sequence inputs are genuinely present: utr.fa holds 8,084 human 5' untranslated region sequences and the cognate BED files carry 11-nucleotide sequence windows around each site.

a4_units_stated.note: Where numbers exist they are unit-clear: methylation ratio as a 0-1 fraction in 5UTRNmPlus1Sites.xlsx, raw ribosome-profiling read counts in the P-site table (data dictionary sheet included).

a5_enough_rows.note: The paper's own labelled measurements total roughly 8 Kozak positions x 2-3 reporters x 3-4 replicates (a few dozen numbers). The largest file carrying a measured value for a 2'-O-methylation site is 5UTRNmPlus1Sites.xlsx with 151 + 181 = 332 rows (65 shared). Both are far under the 1,500-row (or 400 for classification) bar.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~25 MB of tables plus 2.8 MB of sequence; the 465 MB GEO coverage archive is not needed
a6_fits_laptop.note: Everything I opened fits in memory easily; verified by loading all files on this laptop.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Counts I verified agree with the text: ~40% (65/151) of HeLa 5'UTR Nm[+1] sites shared with C4-2 matches the paper's '65 sites (~40%)'.

a8_label_provenance.note: The only table with thousands of 2'-O-methylation rows (23,753 HeLa / 24,272 C4-2 sites) comes from nanopore direct-RNA sequencing calls that the paper itself describes as the 'predicted modification ratio' from a machine-learning classifier (Li et al. 2024), so training on them would distil another model, not measure biology. The one large measured table in the repository (23,327 initiation-site counts) is re-used from a different paper, Arango et al. 2022 Molecular Cell (PMID 35679869).

existing_models.name: Nmix (2024, Briefings in Bioinformatics) - deep learning predictor of 2'-O-methylation (Nm) sites in human RNA
existing_models.score_and_split: Authors report large precision gains over prior tools and 93.8% recovery of experimentally verified rat Nm sites (cross-species test); I read the abstract, not the code.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Generalisation across species and extreme class imbalance between modified and unmodified positions.

existing_models.name: 2OMe-LM (2025, Bioinformatics) - RNA language-model-based 2'-O-methylation site predictor
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported to beat deep-learning baselines on human Nm benchmark sets; metric and split taken from the abstract only.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Transfer to new cell types and to low-stoichiometry sites.

existing_models.name: Meta-2OM (2024, PLOS One) and NmSEER V2.0 (2019) - classical machine-learning Nm site predictors
existing_models.score_and_split: Benchmark-set classification accuracy on curated human Nm sites; splits are sequence-window based, not site-cluster based.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Dependence on which experimental Nm map is used as ground truth.

existing_models.name: TIS Transformer / RiboTIE (NAR Genomics and Bioinformatics 2023; Nature Communications 2025) - transformer models that predict translation initiation sites across the human transcriptome
existing_models.score_and_split: TIS Transformer reports mean precision-recall area under the curve 0.839 for remapping the human proteome, evaluated on held-out chromosomes.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Distinguishing genuinely translated upstream open reading frames at near-cognate (non-AUG) start codons.

existing_models.name: Optimus 5-Prime (Nature Biotechnology 2019) - convolutional network predicting ribosome load from 5' untranslated region sequence
existing_models.score_and_split: Explains 93% of variance in mean ribosome load on 20,000 held-out random 5' untranslated regions; random split of a synthetic library.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Transfer from random synthetic 5' untranslated regions to native human ones.

backbone.name: Nucleotide Transformer / RNA-FM (RNA and DNA language models) would fit the sequence-window input
backbone.hardware: CPU-only laptop would suffice for a few thousand short windows
backbone.licence: Open weights for both, but irrelevant here because there is no usable label table

integration.partner_dataset: RMBase / MODOMICS (catalogues of RNA modification sites) plus GENCODE annotation, joinable on genome coordinates (GRCh38) and gene symbol
integration.join_key: chromosome + position + strand (GRCh38), gene symbol, UCSC transcript ID
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does 2'-O-methylation near start codons explain which upstream near-cognate codons are used for translation initiation across human transcripts? - a real question, but it cannot be answered from these files because the methylation labels are themselves nanopore model calls and the translation readout for methylated sites is measured for only a handful of reporters.

controls.positive_control: Would exist in principle: the model should recover the paper's headline effect that methylation at the first nucleotide of AUG blocks initiation - but with only a few dozen measured values this is the dataset, not a control.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is runnable on the 332-row 5'UTR site table, but that table is too small to learn from.
controls.external_validation: The C4-2 prostate cancer cell line map versus the HeLa map (65 shared 5'UTR sites) gives a cross-cell-line check, and the ribosome-profiling data in GSE105248 gives an independent translation readout.

honest_claim_h3: With these files a model could at best claim: 'given nanopore-predicted 2'-O-methylation calls in two cell lines, sequence context predicts which positions were called modified' - which restates another model's output rather than any measured effect on translation.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use sequence around a start codon to predict whether adding a chemical methyl mark there blocks protein production.
plain_idea.train_on: Intended input: the 11-nucleotide window around each candidate start codon in a human 5' untranslated region, plus the position of the methyl mark relative to the codon. Verified counts: 332 methylated 5'UTR sites with a stoichiometry value, 23,327 ribosome-profiling initiation sites, 8,084 5'UTR sequences.
plain_idea.predict: Intended output: how much protein the transcript makes with versus without the methyl mark. The true answer in this paper comes from luciferase luminescence and green-fluorescent-protein flow cytometry on synthetic messenger RNAs - roughly a few dozen measurements, reported only in figures.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Messenger RNA therapeutic designers would use a rule for where a methyl mark silences or redirects initiation; even a negative result would tell the field whether published methylation maps carry any translation-relevant signal.

more_or_better_data.why: Existing 2'-O-methylation predictors (Nmix, 2OMe-LM, Meta-2OM) train on curated human Nm site sets; this paper adds 332 measured-ratio 5'UTR sites and re-uses the same nanopore maps, so there is no data advantage.

confidence_score.why: The only replication available is HeLa versus C4-2 overlap at 65 shared sites, which is too few to calibrate per-prediction confidence, and the sequencing series GSE341562 has just 2 samples.

models_beatable.why: NmSEER V2.0 (2019, random forest on sequence windows) is old and used window-level splits, so it is beatable in principle - but beating it needs an independent Nm label set, which this paper does not provide.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition: no existing model can be run as a baseline on the quantity this paper measures (protein output under site-specific methylation), because that quantity exists for only a few dozen synthetic reporters and not as a downloadable column.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predict, from the sequence window around a human start codon, whether a 2'-O-methyl mark at a given position inhibits translation initiation - with the paper's reporter measurements as labels. Rejected because those measurements exist only as a few dozen values in figures. The fallback projects (predict nanopore-called methylation sites from sequence; predict initiation-site usage from 5'UTR sequence) either distil another model's calls or re-use a different paper's dataset in a field already served by TIS Transformer and RiboTIE.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from files I actually loaded: ~25 MB of tables and a 2.8 MB fasta all parse in seconds on this laptop; a frozen RNA language model over ~25,000 short windows would be about an hour on CPU. Nothing was timed beyond the loads.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the paper's own measured values: roughly 8 Kozak positions x 2-3 reporters x 3-4 replicates, all reported as bar charts - that count alone kills the project in ten minutes.

verdict_reason: Fails A5, A2 and A8. This is a careful mechanism paper whose measured readout - protein output when a single 2'-O-methyl group sits at a defined position near the start codon - covers only a few dozen synthetic reporter constructs, and those numbers appear only in figures, never as a downloadable column. The only large tables in the authors' repository are (i) 23,753 HeLa and 24,272 C4-2 methylation sites that are a nanopore machine-learning classifier's own predictions, which would mean distilling that model, and (ii) 23,327 ribosome-profiling initiation sites re-used from a different paper (Arango et al. 2022, PMID 35679869) in a task already served by TIS Transformer, RiboTIE and TITER. Its new sequencing series GSE341562 has 2 samples and 465 MB of coverage tracks, not a feature/label table.
